title: Mining Intrinsic Rewards from LLM Hidden States for Efficient Best-of-N Sampling

problem.claim: Best-of-N sampling is limited by its dependence on massive text-based reward models that are computationally expensive and data-hungry.

gap.claim: Existing reward models overlook information available in the LLM's internal hidden states.

contributions.claim: SWIFT learns a reward function directly from information embedded in LLM hidden states.
SWIFT uses simple linear layers at the token embedding level to distinguish preferred from dispreferred generations without text-based modeling.
SWIFT supports compatibility with certain closed-source models via logit access and combination with traditional reward models.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SWIFT as a novel and lightweight method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on standard benchmarks show SWIFT outperforming existing baselines.
The authors report 12.7% higher accuracy than EurusRM-7B on the MATH dataset.
The authors report that SWIFT uses less than 0.005% of the parameters of the compared baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Best-of-N sampling is constrained by expensive, data-hungry text-based reward models.
Existing models do not use the LLM's internal hidden states as a readily available data source.
SWIFT learns intrinsic rewards from hidden states using lightweight linear layers over token embeddings.
The authors report improved benchmark accuracy with substantially fewer parameters.
The authors highlight scalability, selected closed-source-model compatibility, and combination with traditional reward models.

unknowns: Which benchmarks, models, training data, and evaluation protocols were used beyond the reported MATH comparison.
How SWIFT's performance varies across closed-source models and logit-access conditions.
The meaning of the reported parameter percentage and the specific baselines included.
